name: @dropl/mcp

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Shows the connected Dropl account, user, role, API key (name, prefix, scopes, site restriction) and web app URL. Use it to check the connection.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Lists the client sites (websites) this key can reach, with their domains and the plan's site allowance.

tools.name: create_site
tools.description: Creates a client site (one per client website). Check list_sites first to avoid duplicates. Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation. Safe to retry: the same name and domain return the same site.

name.description: Client or website name, e.g. "Acme Builders".

tools.name: list_showcases
tools.description: Lists a client site's showcases (photo/video galleries), newest first.

tools.name: create_showcase
tools.description: Creates a showcase (an embeddable photo/video gallery) in a client site. Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation. Turn on showCategoryFilters when items will be grouped into categories. Safe to retry with the same arguments.

siteId.description: Client site id from list_sites or create_site.

gridFit.description: cover crops grid tiles; contain letterboxes them to show the whole item.

showCategoryFilters.description: Show category filter tabs above the items.

pageSize.description: Items per "Load more" page (3–100), or null to show everything.

tools.name: get_showcase
tools.description: Summarizes a showcase: settings, item counts by status (processing/ready/failed) and kind, categories with counts, and failed items.

tools.name: update_showcase
tools.description: Changes a showcase's title, layout, grid fit, category filter tabs, or page size.

gridFit.description: cover crops grid tiles; contain letterboxes them to show the whole item.

pageSize.description: Items per "Load more" page (3–100), or null to show everything.

tools.name: create_category
tools.description: Adds a category (filter tab) to a showcase. If one with the same name or slug exists, it's returned instead of creating a duplicate.

slug.description: URL form, e.g. kitchen-remodels; derived from the name if omitted.

tools.name: tag_items
tools.description: Adds and/or removes categories on showcase items (photos or videos; item ids come from get_showcase or upload results). Category names that don't exist yet are created.

tools.name: upload_photos
tools.description: Uploads local photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC; up to 20 MB each) into a showcase, straight to storage. Accepts files, folders (recursive by default) and globs; skips hidden files and validates file contents. Run with dryRun: true first and show the result to the user; Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation. Resumable: re-running with the same arguments skips files already uploaded. categoryFromFolder tags each photo with its top-level folder's name; categories tags every photo (both created if missing).

showcaseId.description: Showcase id from create_showcase or list_showcases.

paths.description: Files, folders, or glob patterns (e.g. /abs/photos/**/*.jpg). Prefer absolute paths; relative ones resolve against cwd.

cwd.description: Absolute path of the user's project folder; relative paths resolve against it.

categoryFromFolder.description: Tag photos with their top-level folder name as a category (default false).

categories.description: Category names to tag every uploaded photo with.

dryRun.description: Only check the files and report what would be uploaded.

tools.name: list_videos
tools.description: Lists videos in a client site's library (newest first), optionally filtered by a title search. Use it to find video ids for embeds or showcases.

tools.name: upload_videos
tools.description: Uploads local videos (MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, AVI, MPEG, M4V) to a client site's library in resumable parts, titled from their file names. With showcaseId, also adds them to that showcase (and applies categories / categoryFromFolder). Run with dryRun: true first; Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation. Re-running with the same arguments resumes interrupted uploads and skips finished ones.

paths.description: Files, folders, or glob patterns (e.g. /abs/photos/**/*.jpg). Prefer absolute paths; relative ones resolve against cwd.

cwd.description: Absolute path of the user's project folder; relative paths resolve against it.

showcaseId.description: Showcase (in the same site) to add the videos to.

categoryFromFolder.description: With showcaseId: tag each video with its top-level folder name.

categories.description: With showcaseId: categories to tag every video with.

dryRun.description: Only check the files and report what would be uploaded.

tools.name: add_videos_to_showcase
tools.description: Adds existing library videos (from the showcase's client site) to a showcase. Videos already in it are skipped.

tools.name: get_embed_code
tools.description: Returns the official embed snippet for a video (videoId) or a showcase (showcaseId, optionally one category by name or slug), plus where and how to paste it (plain HTML, React/Next.js, WordPress, Webflow, Framer). Always use this instead of writing embed HTML by hand.

category.description: With showcaseId: a category name or slug, to embed only that category without filter tabs.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Shows storage and bandwidth used against the plan's limits this period, and whether uploads or playback are suspended.

tools.name: plan_migration
tools.description: Scans a local folder (no upload) and proposes how to bring it into Dropl: top-level folders become categories, photo/video counts and sizes per folder, unsupported files by reason, upload batches, whether it needs several showcases, remaining storage (when signed in) and the tool calls to run. Run this first and show the plan to the user for confirmation.

path.description: Folder to scan; prefer an absolute path.

cwd.description: Absolute path of the user's project folder; relative paths resolve against it.

categoryFromFolder.description: Turn top-level folders into categories (default true).

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: Lists a client site's collections (menus, inventory, events, …) with item counts, when a website last read each one, and the plan's item and collection limits.

trashed.description: List trashed collections instead (restorable for 30 days).

tools.name: get_collection_schema
tools.description: Reads a collection's current fields, schemaVersion, and site time zone, including edits made in the dashboard. Always call this before planning a change and pass its schemaVersion as expectedSchemaVersion.

tools.name: plan_collections
tools.description: Dry run: previews creating or changing up to 10 collections on a client site and returns a plain-text diff (fields added, renamed, removed, items affected). Nothing is saved. Show the summary to the user before apply_collection_plan.

slug.description: Matches an existing collection of the site; otherwise a new one gets this slug.

templateKey.description: Start a new collection from a template when fields are omitted.

key.description: Existing fields: always send their current key (from get_collection_schema). New fields: omit; it's derived from the label.

value.description: Stored value; derived from the label when omitted. Keep existing values unchanged.

min.description: number, price (amount), or text length limits.

titleFieldKey.description: Key of the field shown as each item's title.

visibility.description: public (default) can be read by the website without a key.

expectedSchemaVersion.description: Required to change an existing collection: the schemaVersion you read with get_collection_schema.

tools.name: apply_collection_plan
tools.description: Creates or changes the collections previewed with plan_collections. Destructive changes are refused unless confirmDestructive is true, and a collection edited since its expectedSchemaVersion is refused as a conflict. Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation.

slug.description: Matches an existing collection of the site; otherwise a new one gets this slug.

templateKey.description: Start a new collection from a template when fields are omitted.

key.description: Existing fields: always send their current key (from get_collection_schema). New fields: omit; it's derived from the label.

value.description: Stored value; derived from the label when omitted. Keep existing values unchanged.

min.description: number, price (amount), or text length limits.

titleFieldKey.description: Key of the field shown as each item's title.

visibility.description: public (default) can be read by the website without a key.

expectedSchemaVersion.description: Required to change an existing collection: the schemaVersion you read with get_collection_schema.

confirmDestructive.description: Only after the user explicitly agreed to every destructive change in the plan.

tools.name: add_collection_items
tools.description: Bulk-adds items to a collection with per-item errors keyed by field key. Run with dryRun: true (the default) first; saving (dryRun: false) needs explicit confirmation. Accepts up to 2000 items, sent in batches; retrying the same call doesn't duplicate items.

values.description: Values keyed by field key (see get_collection_schema).

mode.description: valid_only (default) saves the valid items; all_or_nothing saves nothing if any item is invalid.

tools.name: list_collection_items
tools.description: Lists a collection's items, drafts included, with search, status and field filters, sorting, and paging.

operator.description: eq (default) matches any of comma-separated values.

sort.description: position (default), createdAt, updatedAt, publishedAt, title, or a field key; prefix - for descending.

tools.name: get_collection_code
tools.description: Returns TypeScript types and a Next.js fetch example generated from the collection's current fields, plus its public items URL. Use this instead of guessing the response shape.

tools.name: undo_collection_change
tools.description: Undoes the most recent schema change of a collection (or the given activity entry) when no data written since would be lost. Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation.

activityId.description: Activity entry to undo; defaults to the most recent undoable one.

tools.name: list_feedback
tools.description: Lists feedback the client left on their website (comments on elements, text changes, general notes), newest first. Defaults to open and in progress. Text changes (type text_change) give the current and the exact new wording; they can usually be applied directly in the code (search the project for currentText). Use get_feedback for the full context of one request.

page.description: Only requests on pages whose path contains this, e.g. /menu.

tools.name: get_feedback
tools.description: Gets one feedback request with its full context: page URL, the clicked element (CSS selector, tag, nearby text, position), device and viewport, screenshot and photo URLs (temporary; fetch them to look), and the thread. Text changes (type text_change) give the current and the exact new wording; they can usually be applied directly in the code (search the project for currentText). If a request is ambiguous, reply_to_feedback asking the client to clarify instead of guessing.

tools.name: reply_to_feedback
tools.description: Replies in a feedback request's thread as the signed-in user; the client gets the reply by email. If a request is ambiguous, reply_to_feedback asking the client to clarify instead of guessing. Keep replies short and plain (no code). Safe to retry: the same reply isn't posted twice.

tools.name: update_feedback_status
tools.description: Sets a feedback request to open, in_progress, done, or wont_do. After fixing a request, mark it done with update_feedback_status and a short note saying what changed (the client gets it by email). Marking done emails the client; only mark done once the fix is in the code (and deployed, if the user says so).

resolutionNote.description: Short note for done or wont_do, e.g. "Updated the opening hours on the contact page."

instructions:
Dropl hosts photo/video showcases and videos that web studios embed on their clients' websites. These tools create client sites and showcases in the user's Dropl account, upload local photos and videos, and return embed code.

Rules:
- Before creating a site or showcase or uploading anything, run plan_migration (or upload_photos / upload_videos with dryRun: true), show the plan to the user (client site, showcase title, categories, file counts and sizes) and get their explicit confirmation. Don't create or upload on your own initiative.
- Prefer existing client sites and showcases (list_sites, list_showcases) over creating duplicates.
- Never ask the user to paste an API key into the chat. If a tool says you're not signed in, ask the user to run `npx -y @dropl/mcp login` in their own terminal (or set DROPL_API_KEY in this server's MCP config), then try again.
- Pass absolute paths (or set cwd to the project folder) for uploads.
- Uploads are resumable and idempotent: if one stops partway, run the same call again; finished files are skipped.
- Use get_embed_code for embed snippets; never write embed HTML by hand.
- After adding an embed to the user's project, run the project's build (or type check) to make sure it still compiles.

Collections (structured content like menus, inventory, and events that clients edit in the dashboard):
- Always read the current fields with get_collection_schema before changing a collection. Clients and teammates edit in the dashboard, so your earlier copy may be stale. Never revert or overwrite their edits.
- Run plan_collections first (it never saves), show the summary to the user, and only call apply_collection_plan after their explicit confirmation. Pass confirmDestructive: true only after they agree to every change marked destructive.
- Keep existing field keys and option values exactly; rename only labels. Websites read the keys.
- Import items with add_collection_items and dryRun: true first; fix or report per-item errors before saving.
- Use get_collection_code for the website's TypeScript types and fetch code instead of guessing the response shape. Only published items reach the website.

Feedback (requests clients leave on their website). To fix the open Dropl feedback:
1. list_sites to find the site, then list_feedback (open and in progress by default).
2. get_feedback for each request: page, element selector and nearby text, device, screenshot, and the thread.
3. Text changes (type text_change) give the current and the exact new wording; they can usually be applied directly in the code (search the project for currentText).
4. If a request is ambiguous, reply_to_feedback asking the client to clarify instead of guessing.
5. After fixing a request, mark it done with update_feedback_status and a short note saying what changed (the client gets it by email).
Tell the user which requests you fixed, which you asked about, and which you skipped.
